youtube.title: Why Padlocks Have a Tiny Hole at the Bottom 🔒 #Shorts
youtube.description:
That tiny hole at the bottom of many padlocks is a drain. Padlocks sit outside in the rain, and water that seeps in around the shackle would otherwise stay trapped, rusting the springs and pins or freezing and jamming the lock. The hole lets it drain out, and it's also a handy spot to drip in a little lubricant.

Subscribe to The Hidden Why for a new why every day.

#Shorts #science #facts #thehiddenwhy

sources: Master Lock FAQ: the drain hole on the bottom of outdoor padlocks lets water escape to prevent rust and freezing
Locksmith guidance: lubricate a padlock through its keyway/drain hole with dry graphite or light oil
